Adolescent gynecology focuses on the reproductive health and well-being of teenage girls and young women. It addresses various gynecological concerns, educates adolescents about their bodies, and provides guidance on maintaining optimal reproductive health.
Adolescence is a crucial time for understanding and managing your reproductive health.

Providers who are skilled in adolescent gynecology work to make sure young women receive accurate information about their changing bodies, menstrual health, contraception, sexually transmitted infections (STIs), and other vital aspects of reproductive well-being.
At what age should you start visiting a gynecologist?

An adolescent should consider visiting a gynecologist between the ages of 10 and 15, or when she becomes sexually active, whichever comes first. Regular visits help establish a relationship with the gynecologist and ensure that young women receive the necessary guidance for a healthy transition into adulthood.

Sellwood Medical Clinic provides expert guidance on menstrual health management, including irregular periods, heavy bleeding, and painful periods. Early detection and treatment are critical for preventing long-term health complications.

primary-care: Primary care is the starting point for a happy and healthy life. The team at Sellwood Medical Clinic includes some of the best primary care specialists in the region, and with three offices in Portland, Oregon, access to the experienced team is never far away. If you’re searching for an outstanding primary care physician, schedule an appointment today online or over the phone.

Primary care is an area of medical specialty that focuses on delivering the preventive, diagnostic, and treatment services you need to thrive. It can be thought of as the foundation on which all aspects of your health are built.

Don’t make the mistake of postponing visits with your primary care physician until something goes wrong. You’ll miss out on many of the benefits of working in partnership with a skilled medical professional.
What services does a primary care physician provide?

Your primary care physician handles your annual physical exams. This allows your doctor to assess your current health and wellness and add relevant data to your medical record. The importance of this record cannot be overstated.
If you notice symptoms or changes over time, your primary care physician can review your medical record and look for trends that could suggest the cause.
If you’ve had treatment for a chronic health condition, your medical record shows which treatments worked and which did not.
How can my primary care physician improve my quality of life?
Preventive health is an undervalued aspect of primary care. Your doctor views their role as your partner in health and wellness.
The more information you share with your primary care physician, the better equipped they are to shape your care.

For example, a woman who is training for a half-marathon and is also planning to start a family in the coming year could benefit from a discussion about the best training and diet options to support both of those goals.

A man in middle age who is experiencing decreased sex drive and has put on a significant amount of weight has a completely different set of health needs. A discussion about hormone replacement therapy and lifestyle changes can make a world of difference.

If you don’t have a primary care physician to guide you through your health and wellness needs, consider coming in to meet the Sellwood Medical Clinic team. You can set up a visit online or over the phone today.

flu-shots: Today, more than ever, it’s easy to see the frightening power of viruses. Fortunately, there’s an easily accessible vaccine for influenza, the virus that causes up to 45 million illnesses in the United States every year. At Sellwood Medical Clinic with four locations in the greater metro Portland, Oregon, the dedicated team of medical specialists makes getting the flu vaccination easier than ever.
Do I need a flu shot?

Yes, and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends flu shots for everyone starting at 6 months old. In extremely rare circumstances, certain individuals don’t need a flu shot, but this is generally confined to those with potentially fatal allergies to the flu vaccine.
An annual flu vaccination is a potentially life-saving measure that you can easily access, so it makes sense to protect yourself to the maximum degree possible.
What does the flu vaccine protect me from?
The flu vaccine is different every year because influenza occurs in many strains.
The vaccine is always formulated to fight the three or four strains of influenza that research predicts as the most common in the US during a particular flu season.
Does the flu vaccine fight COVID-19?
No, because influenza and COVID-19 are two entirely different types of viruses.
When a COVID-19 vaccine is available, that vaccine will protect only against COVID-19, so you’ll need to continue with yearly flu shots as well.
Could you get COVID-19 and the flu at the same time?
Yes, you could potentially develop COVID-19 and the flu at the same time. The CDC predicts that both viruses will spread in the fall and winter months.
Because of this, getting your flu shot is more essential than ever this year.
When is the best time to get flu shots?

The months of September and October are the ideal times to get a flu shot, as that’s when the virus starts circulating. Sellwood Medical Clinic starts the drive-thru flu shots clinic on Saturday, August 29th, and continues with weekly clinics every Saturday until they run out of flu vaccines.
newborn-care/newborn-circumcision-care: Circumcision is an elective procedure that removes the foreskin from the penis of male newborns

We perform this surgical procedure for infants up to 14 days old who have already received their vitamin K shot. We do our best to keep patients calm and comfortable during the procedure, including a secure swaddle, sucrose water (sugar water), and local anesthetic (numbing medication).
Please plan for the visit to take up to two hours, including a monitoring period following the procedure to watch for any bleeding (30-45 minutes).

Your baby’s penis will be red and swollen for several days. A moist, yellowish film may appear around the head of the circumcised penis as it’s healing—this is called granulation tissue and it’s normal. Don’t try to wipe it off!
Your baby’s scrotum or skin around the penis may be bruised from the circumcision for several days.
Healing of the circumcision usually takes seven to 10 days. When healing is complete, the head of the penis will look like normal skin.

Your newborn boy may be fussier over the next day after his circumcision, but he should be consolable and continue feeding regularly. You may give your baby infant Tylenol (acetaminophen) only ONE time after his circumcision—his dose is 1.25 ml four to six hours after the circumcision occurred.
Expect the amount of blood on the front of the diaper to be dime-sized or smaller over the first day.
There is any bright red bleeding or oozing, or if the amount of blood on the front of the diaper is larger than the size of a quarter.
Your baby does not urinate within eight hours after the circumcision.
The redness and swelling around the head of the penis is getting worse.
There is thick, smelly, yellow or green discharge.

Any fever greater than or equal to 100.4° F. We recommend taking a rectal or axillary (armpit) temperature if your baby is fussier than usual, less active than usual, seems warm, or is not feeding at his baseline.
Your baby seems very fussy after one day.
family-medicine-clinic: Finding a qualified family medicine provider can be a challenge, but Sellwood Medical Clinic provides top-notch care for both adults and children. They offer comprehensive preventive care and family medicine services to your whole family. If you need help managing an illness, your expert provider offers personalized attention.

Looking for a new physician can be a confusing process. Some doctors call themselves internal medicine physicians. Others refer to themselves as family medicine practitioners. You might wonder if there’s a difference.

In general, doctors who specialize in internal medicine care for adults, while family practitioners serve adults and children. With a family medicine doctor, your whole family can receive care from the same provider. These doctors are often ideal providers for parents of young children.
What does a family medicine doctor do?

Family practitioners do a little bit of everything. They provide a variety of preventive care services to keep your family healthy. Your provider does valuable health screenings to diagnose problems early on. They also take care of you when you’re sick or injured. Sellwood Medical Clinic providers offer a wide range of services, including:

Your provider does regular checkups to keep you in good health. They also provide your children with top-notch care. Your child can receive important screenings, vaccines, and sports physicals. And if anyone in your family gets sick, your provider delivers the care they need to feel better.
How often should I see my doctor?

All adults should receive annual physical exams. Children over 3 need yearly exams as well. But babies and toddlers need to see the doctor more frequently. Your provider can help you schedule visits for every member of your family. If you’re not feeling well, don’t hesitate to call the office. There’s no need to wait until your next exam. The Sellwood Medical Clinic team is always ready to provide care.
What happens if I need specialized care?
Sometimes your provider will recommend visiting a specialist. Specialists offer care of complex health conditions like cancer and heart disease.
If you need to see a specialist, Sellwood Medical Clinic helps you choose the right one. They also offer follow-up appointments to make sure you’re feeling better.
Looking for a new family practitioner? Call Sellwood Medical Clinic today or schedule an appointment online.

The clinic’s expert providers specialize in family medicine and pediatrics. No matter what health challenges you face, they provide top-notch care with three convenient offices throughout the Portland, Oregon, area. If your child needs to see a doctor, don’t delay.
Why are regular exams so important?

Routine visits are essential to keep your child healthy. Physical exams allow Sellwood Medical Clinic providers to chart your child’s growth. These visits also include valuable screenings like hearing and vision tests.
During their physical exam, your child receives immunizations and other preventive care. Each well-child visit also provides practitioners with essential information about your child’s development.

What will happen during my child's exam?

During a well-child visit, your provider checks your child’s weight and height. They might also ask whether your child has met certain developmental milestones. This information helps your provider determine if your child is healthy. Your provider might ask questions about your child’s social behavior, learning, diet, and lifestyle. Afterward, your child’s hearing and vision may be tested.
Your provider will then do a complete physical exam. In some cases, your provider might suggest follow-up tests like blood work. These tests help identify common childhood health concerns.

Most physical exams result in a clean bill of health. But if your child needs further care, your Sellwood Medical Clinic can help. In some cases, your provider will suggest a visit to a specialist.
